cards.title: Nonlinear Elimination and Mean Residence Time (MRT) Interpretation
cards.claim: In systems with Michaelis-Menten (nonlinear) elimination, the standard moment analysis calculation of MRT (AUMC/AUC) does not equal the true Mean Residence Time. For these systems, Dose/AUC represents a time-average clearance, and the true MRT is a function of the steady-state volume of distribution and this time-average clearance. AUMC/AUC is numerically computable but its interpretation as MRT fails under nonlinear conditions.
conditions: Applicable when drug elimination follows Michaelis-Menten kinetics (capacity-limited saturable elimination).
Requires IV administration into a one- or two-compartment system for the cited derivation.
Not applicable to linear first-order elimination where AUMC/AUC is a valid MRT estimate.
required_inputs: Steady-state volume of distribution (Vss) if available.
limitations: REF_014 is abstract-only; detailed nonlinear formulas are not fully extracted.
The distinction between 'true MRT' and 'moment MRT' is specific to the theoretical framework of the cited study.
This does not prohibit descriptive AUC calculation, but warns against misinterpreting AUMC/AUC as MRT in nonlinear contexts.
cards.downstream_use: Use to select appropriate PK parameters for nonlinear drugs. Avoid using AUMC/AUC as a proxy for MRT in nonlinear models; prefer Dose/AUC for clearance estimation and specific nonlinear MRT derivations if available.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Renal/nonrenal clearance, nonlinear elimination, formulation and route limits

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
